gp.text: Gross Profit: For the year ended December 31, 2024, consolidated gross profit increased $18.6 million, or 10.2%, compared to the prior year period. Gross profit as a percentage of net sales decreased to 55.9% of net sales for the year ended December 31, 2024, from 56.3% of net sales for the year ended December 31, 2023. The overall decrease in gross profit margin was driven primarily by increased sales in modern oral in the Stoker’s products segment and cigars in the Zig-Zag products segment which generates lower margins than other product categories.

oi.text: Other Operating Income: For the year ended December 31, 2024, other operating income decreased $2.7 million compared to the prior year period due to a federal excise tax refund of $1.7 million received in 2024 compared to a $4.3 million federal excise tax refund received in 2023.

ga.text: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses : For the year ended December 31, 2024, selling, general and administrative expenses increased $18.1 million, or 17.3%, compared to the prior year period. Selling, general and administrative expenses for the year ended December 31, 2024, included $7.2 million of stock options, restricted stock and incentives expense, $4.6 million of expense related to corporate restructuring, $3.6 million of expense related to PMTA, $2.1 million related to transaction costs and $0.9 million of expense related to the implementation of the new ERP and CRM systems. Corporate restructuring expense increased in 2024 compared to the prior year period primarily due to a voluntary early retirement program offered to employees in October 2024. This program offered early retirement benefits to employees meeting certain criteria. Agreements with employees were finalized in the fourth quarter of 2024 and the Company booked a $2.7 million reserve for estimated future payments.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text:
For the year ended December 31, 2024, net cash provided by operating activities was $61.0 million, an increase of $4.7 million compared to the prior year period, primarily due to an increase in net income, net of non-cash items of $12.6 million and a favorable change in other assets of $3.1 million, partially offset by a $11.0 million unfavorable change in working capital. The primary drivers of non-cash items were a $9.5 million decrease in loss on investments compared to the prior year period and a $6.5 million decrease in deferred tax expense, partially offset by increases of $1.6 million in depreciation and other amortization expense and a $1.7 million decrease in gains on extinguishment of debt compared to the prior year period.

For the year ended December 31, 2023, net cash provided by operating activities was $56.2 million, an increase of $34.9 million compared to the prior year period, primarily due to an increase in the change in working capital of $35.2 million (net of inventory reserve), partially offset by a decrease in the change in other assets of $5.3 million. The increase in working capital was primarily driven by an increase in the change in inventories of $40.0 million related to the timing of changes in inventory.

da.text: We define “EBITDA” as net income before interest expense, gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt, income tax expense, depreciation, and amortization. We define “Adjusted EBITDA” as net income before interest expense, gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt, income tax expense, depreciation, amortization, other non-cash items, and other items we do not consider the ordinary course in our evaluation of ongoing operating performance noted in the reconciliation below. Among other items that we adjust Adjusted EBITDA for is FDA PMTA expense. The Company believes it is appropriate to adjust for this spend as the costs are incurred in connection with what we view as a non-traditional regulatory process that requires applications be submitted for covered products that are already on the market. As a result, Company’s management believes it is most appropriate to assess the performance of the Company’s business – the sale of our various products - without regard to these costs and believes that adjusting for these costs provides investors and the public markets with the most meaningful metrics to assess performance of the business.

intro.text: Turning Point Brands, Inc. (the “Company,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) is a leading manufacturer, marketer and distributor of branded consumer products. We sell a wide range of products to adult consumers consisting of staple products with our iconic brands Zig-Zag® and Stoker’s®. We primarily compete in the alternative smoking accessories and Other Tobacco Products (“OTP”) industries, among other markets. The alternative smoking accessories market is a dynamic market experiencing robust secular growth driven by cannabinoid legalization in the U.S. and Canada, and positively evolving consumer perception and acceptance in North America. The OTP industry, which consists of non-cigarette tobacco products, exhibited steady consumer unit annualized volumes during the full year period ended 2025 as reported by Management Science Associates, Inc.

We have no borrowings outstanding under our ABL as of December 31, 2025. Our Convertible Senior Notes matured on July 15, 2024, and were retired with cash.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
